title: What We Stopped Believing: 10 Prompt Myths We Tested and Rejected
lede: Ten things we confidently believed about fashion AI prompts — and the experiments that proved us wrong. An exercise in updating beliefs.
body_md:
## Belief 1: More detail is always better
Rejected. Beyond 80 words, added detail averaged into noise in our experiments. We now delete before adding.

## Belief 2: Model-specific 'magic words' transfer
Rejected. Words that worked on 2022 models (ArtStation trending, masterpiece) produced no measurable change on current models. Re-test every assumption after a model generation change.

## Belief 3: Negative prompts are reliable
Partly rejected. 'No blur' is unreliable; describing the desired sharp state is better. Negation works inconsistently across models.

## Belief 4: One perfect prompt exists
Rejected. A prompt is a hypothesis valid for one model, one version, one reference. We now think in terms of frameworks, not magic strings.

## Belief 5-10
(Full article covers: 'Chinese words only for Chinese models', 'higher guidance equals better', 'seeds guarantee reproducibility', 'more reference images help', 'upscale equals detail', 'style words stack linearly'.)

## The value of being wrong
Every rejected belief freed a slot in our mental model for a verified rule. Updating beliefs is the actual work of a prompt lab.
